title: DORA TLPT Requirements Explained: Where Threat Intelligence Fits
content_md: The DORA TLPT requirements push selected EU financial entities beyond standard penetration testing. TLPT must be based on realistic threat scenarios, relevant threat actors, and current intelligence about how attacks are actually carried out. That makes threat intelligence a core part of the process. It helps define what should be tested, which TTPs matter, and which attack paths are most relevant to the organization. Let’s look at the main TLPT requirements explained in practice, where threat intelligence fits into DORA TLPT, and what teams need to get right before testing begins. What Are the DORA TLPT Requirements? The Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), established under Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, sets cybersecurity and operational resilience requirements for financial entities across the European Union. Under DORA Article 26 TLPT , certain financial entities must carry out threat-led penetration testing at least once every three years. The DORA TLPT frequency can be adjusted depending on the entity’s risk profile and operational circumstances. The framework is maintained by the European Central Bank (ECB), while the DORA TLPT standards were developed by the European Supervisory Authorities
